merge.reading: All CISA KEV CVE ids also appear in the EUVD exploited list, plus a few more. That is overlap, not proof of derivation, and EUVD does not say who observed the exploitation: the two are not counted as independent confirmation.

rules.rule: Exploitation is what a source asserts in a structured field. A critical score, a high EPSS value or the word "critical" is severity and never makes a vulnerability "exploited".
Each source keeps its own statement. Two sources asserting exploitation are not called independent confirmation unless the registry says they are independent.

A Linux package is never called vulnerable from upstream version ranges: a distribution backports fixes. Only a distribution advisory for that release and package can say so; otherwise the verdict is NOT_ASSESSED.
Identifiers (CVE, EUVD, GHSA) join records only when a source declares them as its own. Text mentions, reference URLs and similar product names never join records.
Nothing is redistributed until the registry says the licence allows it AND the owner confirmed it. Today no vulnerability source passes both.
